messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync — we need to pick the default chat endpoint shape for the Q2 product launch. Two consistent customer asks: prompt compatibility (legacy SDKs) and a canonical messages array that supports roles + function/tool calling + structured output enforcement. Can we decide today?

maria (PM): TL;DR options: A) messages-first (roles + functions native, no 'prompt' param). B) dual-mode (messages + legacy 'prompt' accepted). C) prompt-first with adapter on the server. Please vote and call out blockers.

jake (Eng): leaning A (messages-first). Runtime is simpler if we standardize on messages+roles. But we need a compatibility shim for existing prompt-based customers — otherwise painful migrations.

anita (ML): +1 to messages-first. Function calling reliability requires us to provide a typed output contract and server-side schema validation. Also want eval hooks for structured-output regressions.

sam (Eng-Platform): caveat: token accounting and batching behavior will differ between prompt vs messages. If we flip default we must update billing telemetry and make diffs visible in Console. Also watch streaming semantics.

renata (Research): we tested both. Messages-first gives cleaner system role enforcement (no implicit system text concatenation) and fewer degenerate completions. However some customers embed long prompts programmatically; dual-mode eases their lift.

claire (CS): FinTech customer (Acct: fintech-x) explicitly asked for: 1) enforced system role that can't be overridden by user messages, 2) server-side audit logs of system messages, 3) structured JSON responses for downstream parsing. They prefer messages-first but want a migration window.

oliver (Legal): For Private deployments we need immutability & retention policies for system role logs. If system messages are enforced server-side we must document who can change them (RBAC).

maria (PM): Proposed decision + rollout plan: default = messages-first on hosted API. Provide a compatibility header X-Redwood-Compat: prompt to accept legacy 'prompt' param for 6 months. Add an opt-in flag strict_structured_output that enforces schema validation and returns 400 on mismatch. Acceptance criteria before GA: - Streaming parity (no regressions in 95p latency) - Structured-output parse success >= 97% on our eval set - No >2% error-rate increase on top 10 customer flows - Console shows clear token delta for migrated apps

maria (PM): Canary plan: enable messages-first for 5% of traffic, collect metrics for 48h, run automated evals on seeded test prompts, CS-run pilot with FinTech-X. If metrics pass, ramp to 50% then 100%.

jake (Eng): implementation note: backend will accept both shapes but messages will be canonicalized in the router. I'll open an RFC + branch. Branch name proposal: feature/chat-shape/messages-default.

anita (ML): for function calling we should return a structured 'tool_output' object in the response envelope when strict_structured_output=true. That makes downstream parsing deterministic.

renata (Research): we should add a small adapter in the SDKs that converts 'prompt' -> messages(array) with inferred roles so customers get a smooth migration.

sam (Eng-Platform): +1. Also we'll add a Console flag to visualize 'compat mode' token usage per-route.

claire (CS): I'll schedule the FinTech-X pilot for next week and collect example prompts they rely on.

oliver (Legal): Please add RBAC docs for who can set/override system role in Private deployments. I'll review.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/telemetry-compat -> staging (deployer: jake) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria (PM): Decision recap (agreed): messages-first default; compatibility header for prompt mode for 6 months; SDK adapters for migration; opt-in strict_structured_output flag + server schema validation; canary -> ramp plan and acceptance criteria as above. Action items: Jake -> RFC + branch, Sam -> telemetry dashboard, Anita/Renata -> eval suite for structured output, Claire -> pilot w/ FinTech-X, Oliver -> RBAC doc.

jake (Eng): noted. I'll open the RFC today and tag the branch in the thread.

maria (PM): Thanks all :thumbsup:
